tasks.title: The port function mask
tasks.solution: The mask is the sum of 2^bit. Bit 0 is MSP (1), bit 6 is RX_SERIAL (64), bit 4 is LTM (16), bit 9 is IBUS (512). All four combinations are allowed: MSP shares a port with telemetry, the receiver — with LTM or IBUS.

tasks.title: How many MSP ports can be added
tasks.solution: MSP is bit 0, that is, an odd mask. There are no more than three ports with MSP (MAX_MSP_PORT_COUNT), and USB VCP counts. The answer = 3 − the number of odd masks; a negative answer means that on saving the port table is reset to the default.

tasks.title: The nominal MAVLink budget
tasks.solution: Budget = 55·ext + 54·rc + 136·pos + 40·extra1 + 32·extra2 + 94·extra3 + 45. 136 is the three position messages (64 + 40 + 32), 94 is BATTERY_STATUS and SCALED_PRESSURE, 45 is HEARTBEAT and SYSTEM_TIME once a second.

tasks.title: The real stream rate
tasks.solution: The counter is loaded with ⌊50 / r⌋ and fires on the call after zero, and the calls come once every 20 ms: f = 50 / (⌊50 / r⌋ + 1). For 10 Hz that is 8.33 Hz, and it never exceeds 25 Hz.

tasks.title: The msp_override_channels mask
tasks.solution: Bit = channel number − 1: CH1 (roll) is bit 0, CH4 (throttle) is bit 3, CH5 (AUX1) is bit 4. The mask is the sum of 2^(n − 1). The firmware itself excludes the channel that carries the MSP RC OVERRIDE mode.

tasks.title: How long the override holds after the script stops
tasks.solution: 200 ms is the signal timeout of the MSP receiver (5 Hz), then the failure period of 200 ms + failsafe_delay × 100 ms: T = 400 + 100 · failsafe_delay. At the default 5 — 900 ms, and all that time the last values of the script are in effect.

tasks.title: ELRS telemetry bandwidth
tasks.solution: burst = ⌊512 · f / N / 1000⌋ − 1, but no less than 1; bit/s = 5 · 8 · burst · f / N / (burst + 1) with integer division; bytes/s = bit/s / 8. The factor burst / (burst + 1) is the link statistics slot. 250 Hz, 1:64: burst 1, 78 bit/s, 9.75 bytes/s.

tasks.title: LTM headroom on the port baud rate
tasks.solution: The port carries b / 10 bytes/s. 303 bytes/s is NORMAL, 164 is MEDIUM, 105 is SLOW. At 2400 baud the firmware itself replaces NORMAL with MEDIUM, at 1200 — any schedule with SLOW.
